Performers
Mary Garden (soprano), Claude Debussy (piano) Documented

Both performers are named by the archive, national-library catalogue and specialist discography; no unnamed collaborator is supplied.

[1] [2] [3]
Work version
Song for soprano and piano Documented

The performing forces are established. The precise edition, any session-specific alteration and the original sounding pitch are not established. The two-record Garden 1904 set is an archival grouping, not a claim that these extracts form a two-movement composition.

[1] [2] [5]
Recorded
1904 Documented

Only the year is established here; no exact day is inferred from a later reissue or modern repository date.

[1] [2] [3]
Place
Paris, France Documented

The city is documented. The studio, street address and recording engineer are not established.

[1] [3]
Label
Gramophone & Typewriter (G&T) Documented

Original commercial acoustic disc attribution. The 1937 IRCC/RCA carrier catalogued by BnF is a later reissue.

[1] [3]
Catalogue
33449 Documented

Original G&T catalogue number. The archive describes a ten-inch disc.

[1] [3]
Matrix, take, sides
Unknown Disputed: sources disagree

Internet Archive’s 3047II disagrees with the 3074 numbering in the discography and Phonobase. This appears consistent with a transposition error in the archive field, but it is not silently corrected. Suffix forms and the actual source disc’s take remain unresolved.

  • 3047II (Internet Archive metadata, verbatim)
  • 3074F (discography); 3074-ii (Phonobase copy)
[1] [3] [9]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

The archive names an uploader account but does not identify a transfer engineer. Uploader identity is not converted into a recording or mastering credit.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The 2019 added/public dates belong to the repository. No date of digitisation of this copy is established.

[1]
Processing
Playback at 74 rpm; stylus-size field “25”; MP3 access file. Documented

The source supplies no units for the stylus-size string. Equalisation, noise reduction, pitch correction and equipment are not established. The speed is not treated as proof of the original session’s tuning or tempo.

[1]
Composition rights
Underlying composition and original French words are out of copyright under ordinary life-plus-70 terms; the historical score predates 1926. Inferred, not documented

Debussy died in 1918 and Verlaine in 1896. No modern translation is reproduced; national exceptions and modern editions require separate consideration.

[6] [7] [5]
Recording rights
Rule 2 — US public domain: original G&T commercial issue dated 1904, before the 1925 cutoff. Documented

The original G&T catalogue and 1904 attribution establish a pre-cutoff recording publication basis. The 1937 reissue and 2019 archive upload are not used as the original publication date. No free-recording licence is inferred from a composition-only tag.

[1] [3] [8] [9]

Claude Debussy, Il pleure dans mon cœur; Mary Garden, soprano, and Claude Debussy, piano. Paris, 1904; G&T 33449; Internet Archive transfer. US pre-1926 publication basis.

  1. Internet Archive — Il pleure dans mon cœur — G&T catalogue 33449; date 1904; coverage Paris; Mary Garden and Debussy; soprano/piano; ten-inch disc; transfer at 74 rpm; stylus string 25 without stated units. The 2019 repository dates are not session or transfer dates.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  2. Bibliothèque nationale de France — historical Debussy recording catalogue — Subnotice 6 names Mary Garden, soprano, and Claude Debussy, piano, recorded in 1904. Its carrier is the later 1937 RCA/IRCC reissue, not the original G&T disc transferred here.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  3. The Record Collector — International Record Collectors Club discography — IRCC 107: Garden, soprano; Debussy, piano; Paris 1904; matrix 3074F; original G&T 33449; later transfer matrix 0EA5670-1.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  4. Discography of American Historical Recordings — Mary Garden — Performer entry consulted for discographic cross-checking. Its displayed Victor/Columbia records do not establish the French G&T matrix here; no unrelated American matrix or session date is imported.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  5. Debussy — Ariettes oubliées no. 2, voice-and-piano score — Printed pp. 12–⁠17 (PDF 4–⁠9), poem and voice/piano notation inspected visually. Exact edition used at the 1904 session not established.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  6. IMSLP — Claude Debussy biographical dates — Debussy died on 25 March 1918.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  7. IMSLP — Paul Verlaine biographical dates — Verlaine died on 8 January 1896.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  8. United States Copyright Office — Classics Protection and Access Act — Term: recordings first published before 1923 ceased receiving the specified federal remedies after 31 December 2021. The programme also permits publication through 1925 as of 2026.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  9. Phonobase 12051 — Garden/Debussy, G&T 33449 — A separate contemporary acoustic copy, Paris 1904, catalogue GC 33449, matrix 3074-ii, 74 rpm. Phonobase’s 2018 digitisation date belongs to that other copy, not to this IA transfer.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
